14	CASE OD2-HO-ADVERS-1 (ADVERS, cross-domain): Best-improved supplier, worst-performing valve
15	Setting: Brenmoor Heat Systems (fictional) builds AH-series air-source heat pumps, about 4,100 units a month. 18	E1 [stage S1] Email from Marcus Ilvane, VP Operations, to quality leadership, 12 Oct 2026 (leadership-account): Subject: VA-220 claims. Let's not chase the wrong rabbit. I want an installer remediation plan by Friday.
19	E2 [stage S1] Warranty dashboard export, AH-series, 9 Oct 2026 (system-record): VA-220-coded claims within 120 days in service, per 1,000 units, by build month: 2025 average 6; Jan 2026 22; Feb 30; Mar 33; Apr 35; May 34; Jun 21 (120-day window incomplete). Top 2026 claim code: 'reversing valve – capacity loss / internal leak' (82% of VA-220 claims). VA-220 sources in 2026: Pellacott about 80% of volume, Durrant-Hale about 20%. The dashboard does not split claims by valve source, installer or firmware version.
20	E3 [stage S1] SupplierPath scorecard, Pellacott Precision (VA-220) (document): Score = 0.45 × on-site process audit + 0.40 × submitted test-record conformance + 0.15 × delivery. Test-record conformance = percentage of lot certificates that carry complete per-piece leak values with every piece within the stated limit. Dock-to-stock is granted automatically at 85 or above. Q4 2025 baseline: 74 / 58 (per-piece leak values missing on 9 of 14 certificates) / 88 = 70. Q1 2026 (document review 31 Mar): 76 / 92 / 88 = 84. Q2 (2 Jul): 78 / 100 / 90 = 89, dock-to-stock granted. Q3 (30 Sep): 79 / 100 / 90 = 89. Programme note: across all 22 SupplierPath suppliers, average test-record conformance went from 71 (Q4 2025) to 96 (Q3 2026).
21	E4 [stage S1] Pellacott Precision process change notice PCN-25-118, 2 Dec 2025 (vendor-account): Part: VA-220. Changes take effect from the first 2026 production run (12 Jan 2026): (1) the internal slide seal will come from Corlin Polymer instead of Ferrand Elastomers, at lower cost (Ferrand remains an approved source); (2) VA-220 assembly moves from Line 1 to the new Line 3. Validation: 30 Corlin seals checked for dimensions and hardness. The 100% end-of-line pressure-decay leak test on rig LT-04 is unchanged. Approved by the Brenmoor supplier quality engineer on 15 Dec 2025.
22	E5 [stage S1] Notes of call with Renata Oduya, Field Service Manager, 8 Oct 2026 (manager-account): 'My techs are replacing more VA-220s on jobs done by the new installer firms. That's the pattern they report.' The new firms work mostly on new-build housing estates, so nearly all their installs are 2026-built units. Legacy firms do more replacements of older stock. She also flagged firmware 4.2 (over-the-air from 10 Mar), which cut minimum compressor off-time from 180 s to 90 s, 'so more valve shifts'. Units without the connectivity module (about a quarter) stay on 4.1. She has not formally split failures by installer or by firmware.
23	E6 [stage S1] Pellacott certificate of conformance, lot P26-0731, as uploaded to the SupplierPath portal (document): Part VA-220, lot P26-0731, quantity 800, build date 21 Jul 2026. Test: 100% pressure-decay leak test at 24 bar, limit 5.0 Pa/min, rig LT-04 (calibration due 30 Nov 2026). Per-piece results table attached (800 values), range 0.6–1.9 Pa/min; 800/800 pass. Operator: K.D. Signed: S. Mirek, Quality Manager. Shipment paperwork carries only a one-line lot pass statement. Per-piece certificates are uploaded to the portal in batches for SupplierPath document review.
24	CATALOGUE (full contents)
25	C1 [stage S1] Installer onboarding and training records, firms onboarded Feb–Apr 2026 - Brenmoor installer network team (document): All 14 installer firms added Feb–Apr 2026 completed Brenmoor's 3-day AH-series certification: refrigerant handling, brazing with nitrogen purge, evacuation to 500 microns, commissioning. Spot audits of first installs: 11 firms had no findings; 3 firms had one minor finding each (incomplete commissioning checklist ×2, missing evacuation printout ×1). New firms installed about 35% of 2026 AH-series units. Legacy firms over the same period: 4 minor findings across 31 firms.
26	C2 [stage S1] Firmware 4.2 change record and validation summary, March 2026 - Brenmoor controls engineering (change-record): Change record FW-4.2, approved 2 Mar 2026, over-the-air rollout from 10 Mar. Units without a connectivity module cannot receive the update and remain on 4.1.
27	C3 [stage S1] SupplierPath on-site audit reports for Pellacott, Q2 and Q3 2026 - Brenmoor supplier quality (document): Q2 audit on site 2 Jul (announced 20 Jun); Q3 audit 30 Sep (announced 12 Sep). Line 3 VA-220 was not running on either audit day ('changeover to HX-3 build'), so the end-of-line test was not witnessed. Minor findings: two unsigned training records; one faded gauge label.
28	C4 [stage S1] Pellacott written response to Brenmoor warranty concern, 6 Oct 2026 - S. 32	C8 [stage S1] SupplierPath programme scores, all 22 suppliers, Q4 2025–Q3 2026 - SupplierPath portal (system-record): Average overall score went from 74 to 86. Next scheduled scoring cycle (Q4 2026) closes 18 Dec 2026.
33	C9 [stage S1] Purchasing records: Pellacott VA-220 contract terms and volumes, 2025–2026 - Brenmoor procurement (financial-record): Contract renewed 5 Jan 2026: unit price cut 4% in exchange for Pellacott's VA-220 share rising from 70% to 80%. Durrant-Hale holds a 20% share at a unit price 6% above Pellacott's.
34	C10 [stage S1] Calibration contractor site-visit report, Pellacott leak-test rigs, 8 October 2026 - Metrova Calibration Ltd, engaged by Brenmoor under supply-agreement clause 9.4 (independent-observation): Rig LT-04 found disconnected and tagged 'OUT OF SERVICE – pressure transducer failed 9 Jan 2026'. 36	C12 [stage S1] Heating degree-day data, winter 2025–26 against five-year average - National meteorological service (external-data): November 2025 to March 2026: heating degree-days 4% above the five-year average. 37	C13 [stage S1] Interview notes: Brenmoor supplier quality engineer for Pellacott, 14 Oct 2026 - Priya Lunde, SQE (staff-account): 'Pellacott went from our worst paperwork to our best in one quarter, with full per-piece tables on every lot. I didn't ask for rig logs because SupplierPath doesn't require them. Dock-to-stock was automatic once they hit 85.'
38	C14 [stage S1] Customer complaints sample, AH-series, Aug–Sep 2026 - Brenmoor customer service (customer-account): 25 complaints sampled. 18 report loss of heating or 'blowing cool air in heat mode'; 4 report noise; 3 report app connectivity problems. 9 mention the installer favourably and 5 unfavourably. Average time from installation to complaint: 4.5 months. None of the complaints identifies the valve supplier.
39	C15 [stage S1] Brenmoor receiving inspection records, Pellacott VA-220, Jan–Oct 2026 - Brenmoor receiving (system-record): Jan–Jun: per lot, visual and dimensional check on 5 pieces plus a check that a certificate is present. No leak testing at receiving (not in the inspection plan since 2022). 0 rejections. Jul–Sep: dock-to-stock, no receiving checks. 1 Oct: receiving supervisor put six lots on hold after a warranty review meeting; the lots remain in the bonded area.
40	CANDIDATES
41	H1: Installation errors by the installer firms onboarded in 2026 caused the rise in VA-220 field failures.
42	H2: Pellacott's VA-220 valves built in 2026 are defective, and the leak-test certificates Pellacott submitted for them do not reflect tests that were actually performed.
43	H3: Pellacott's VA-220 valves built in 2026 are defective, and Pellacott performed the leak tests its certificates record, but that test method does not detect the defect.
44	H4: Firmware 4.2's shorter minimum compressor off-time caused the rise in VA-220 field failures.
45	H5: Other SupplierPath suppliers have also submitted test records that do not reflect tests that were actually performed.
46	R1: Defects in Pellacott VA-220 valves built in 2026 -> Rise in VA-220 field failures (causes)
47	R2: Onboarding of new installer firms in 2026 -> Rise in VA-220 field failures (causes)
48	R3: Firmware 4.2 rollout -> Rise in VA-220 field failures (causes)
49	R4: Pellacott's switch of slide-seal source to Corlin Polymer -> VA-220 internal seat leakage (causes)
50	R5: Pellacott's submitted test records becoming complete, with every piece shown within the leak limit -> Rise in Pellacott's SupplierPath score (causes)
51	A1: Quarantine all 2026-built Pellacott VA-220 stock (including the six held lots), suspend Pellacott's dock-to-stock status, and release VA-220 stock only after Brenmoor-run helium leak testing.
52	A2: Suspend the certification of the 14 installer firms onboarded in 2026 and charge their VA-220 warranty claims back to them.
53	A3: Release the six held VA-220 lots to production once Pellacott supplies fresh certificates of conformance for them.
54	A4: Instruct Pellacott to go back to Ferrand Elastomers as the slide-seal source for all VA-220 production.
55	A5: Change SupplierPath scoring so that submitted test records earn credit only when backed by rig logs or a witnessed test, starting from the next scoring cycle; all other suppliers' existing dock-to-stock grants remain in place, unverified, until that cycle closes.

answers.justification: C5 matched claim rates for Pellacott 2026 valves are the same for legacy and new installers (41 vs 42), and Durrant-Hale sits at 5–7 in every installer group; brazed joints were intact on all 41 teardowns, never-installed warehouse valves leak at 11% (C5), and C1 shows new firms were trained with few findings, so E1/E5/C4/C6 are confounded by build year.

C10 found LT-04 out of service since 9 Jan 2026 with no test cycle after 18 Dec 2025, no VA-220 program on any other rig and no backup rig, and the 2026 per-piece tables repeat four sequences from Nov 2025, yet E6 claims LT-04 tested a July 2026 lot; C5 shows the 2026 valves are defective.

The tests recorded on the certificates could not have been run, because the only VA-220 rig had been out of service since January and the tables are copied sequences (C10), so 'tested but the method missed the defect' does not fit; C5 notes the pressure-decay method was not replicated, but the tests were never actually done.

C5 shows Pellacott 2026 valves fail at about the same rate on firmware 4.1 (40) and 4.2 (42), Durrant-Hale stays at 5–7 on both, E2 shows the rise had started with Jan–Feb builds before the 10 Mar rollout, and C2 validation found no valve faults.

C8/E3 show that conformance scores rose across the programme (71 to 96) and that no supplier's rig logs are collected, so the claim cannot be ruled out, but no evidence shows fabrication by any supplier other than Pellacott.

Warehouse retest of never-installed valves (C5: Pellacott 2026 11% vs 2025 1% vs Durrant-Hale 0%), teardown showing seal-seat failure matching the dominant claim code (E2), installer, firmware and weather rivals ruled out (C5, C12), a claims-coding artefact excluded (C7), and timing matching the Jan 2026 changes (E4, E2).
C5 shows identical failure rates by installer group for both valve sources, and brazed joints were intact (C5, C6 'no burn marks').
C5 shows no firmware difference within valve source (40 vs 42; Durrant-Hale 5–7 in every group), and the rise starts in builds from before March (E2).

Seal deformation co-occurs with 2026 Corlin-sealed valves (C5, C11 untested compression set and harder-to-softer compound change), but C5 states the Corlin seal and the Line 3 move cannot be separated and the compound was not analysed.

By the E3 formula, conformance rising 58 to 100 at 0.40 weight contributes about 17 of the 19-point gain, while audit (74 to 79) and delivery barely moved, so the score rise follows mechanically from the record change (C13, C8).

With falsified certificates (C10) and an 11% seat-leak rate in uninstalled 2026 stock (C5), containment, suspending dock-to-stock and Brenmoor-run helium testing (which detected the defect in C5) protect the field.
C5 shows installers are not the cause, so suspending installers and charging claims back to them punishes the wrong party (C1 shows they were trained and audited).

Fresh certificates from Pellacott are worthless, because its certificates reflect no actual tests (C10), and about 11% of 2026 lots leak (C5), so releasing the lots would put defective valves into the field.
The seal-source cause is confounded with the Line 3 move and the compound was not analysed (C5, C11), so mandating Ferrand is not yet justified, though it may prove right.

Requiring rig logs or witnessed tests fixes the loophole Pellacott exploited (C8, C13, E3), but leaving 14 other suppliers' dock-to-stock grants unverified until 18 Dec (C8), when the programme verifies no raw test data, keeps a known weakness open, so this is not a best action.

Independent rig observation (C10) plus warehouse retest and matched claim breakdown (C5) are enough to commit to A1 containment and suspension now, even though root cause (seal vs Line 3) is still open.
